source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The EWS OAuth scenario starts with the root folder in allInboxes to avoid connecting during setup. When a connection is expected, waitForMessages discovers Inbox, replaces that shared entry and its local parameter, then checks unread/pending state and server idle before marking read. Bad-token setup first fills the client OAuth cache, then revokeToken deletes server-side validity so retrieval exercises authentication failure. The helper rename does not change token deletion or clear client cache. These are fake-server test boundaries, not real-provider authentication proof. No runtime tests.
title: EWS OAuth retrieval defers Inbox discovery and revokes server validity without clearing the client cache
